body:
Decided with the maintainer on 2026-09-28. One colour scheme for both clients, held in one easily
editable place per client, and the values moved: accent toward the logo's blue end, background flat.

## The scheme (light / dark)

| role | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| background | #FFFFFF | #000000 |
| foreground (text) | #1A1A1E | #F2F2F4 |
| accent (buttons, checkmarks, switches, the selected state) | #5A97FF | #5A97FF |
| highlighted text (links, the "due today" date, emphasised text) | #126BFF | #5A97FF |
| text on accent | #FFFFFF | #0B1220 |

Muted text, borders and secondary surfaces stay neutral greys with no purple tint (web keeps its
#6b6b73 / #e2e2e5 / #f7f7f8 family and their dark twins; Android derives the same greys). The
meaning colours are untouched: error/danger red, balance green (BalancePositive), the checked-item
red. The logo keeps #863BFF → #47BFFF on both clients. The accent no longer tints surfaces:
Android sets surfaceTint to the surface colour (no tonal elevation tint) and background/surface
to pure white/black; the web's --color-bg is already flat.

## Configurable, one place per client

* Web: `web/src/index.css` already holds the tokens; add `--color-accent-strong` (highlighted
  text) and `--color-fg` alias if the naming helps, document the four roles in a comment at the
  top, and use the tokens everywhere the accent or a link colour is set (grep for hard-coded hex in
  src/**/*.css and inline styles: none may remain).
* Android: a new `ui/theme/BrandColors.kt` with the roles above (light and dark objects), from
  which `Theme.kt` builds the Material `lightColorScheme`/`darkColorScheme` (primary = accent,
  onPrimary, background/surface/surfaceContainer* = background or the neutral greys, surfaceTint =
  surface, tertiary = highlighted text where Compose text needs it) — nothing else in ui/ names a
  hex. The dynamic (wallpaper) colour scheme is REMOVED: ThemeVariant loses DYNAMIC_*; the app
  always uses the brand scheme in light and dark.
* Parity test: extend `web/src/lib/balanceColors.test.ts` (which reads Theme.kt) or add a sibling
  that reads BrandColors.kt and asserts the five roles' values equal the web tokens, light and
  dark, so the clients cannot drift.
* READMEs: `android/README.md` (Theme section: the brand scheme, where to change it, no dynamic
  colour) and `web/README.md` (the tokens) describe the scheme, current behaviour only.
* Screens to eyeball after the change (Robolectric screenshot tests are not available; assert
  colours in tests where a colour has meaning): the checked item mark, the selected switch, the
  primary buttons (T-309), the account-section "signed out" banner, the due-today date, the update
  banner, the sync chip, the drawer's selected entry, the login page's brand mark on white.
title: One colour scheme for both clients: flat white/black background, accent #5A97FF with highlighted text #126BFF, held in one configurable place; no wallpaper colours on Android
